Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year, which runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split this between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the allowance between cash, stocks and shares, innovative finance and Lifetime ISAs. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance doesn't carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, people under 65 will be limited to paying £12,000 a year into cash ISAs. That change doesn't affect 2026/27.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Our ISA guide says adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. It doesn't say whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with us, and it doesn't mention children's or junior ISAs. I can't confirm either way from the documents I have.

Please raise this with your adviser. The guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You must be aged 18 to 39 to open one. Withdrawals for reasons other than those below incur a 25% government charge. The no-charge reasons are:
- buying a first home costing £450,000 or less, once the account has been open for at least 12 months
- being aged 60 or over
- being terminally ill with less than 12 months to live

More detail is in the ISAs guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

At 42 you're too old to open a Lifetime ISA. They can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39.

You can still pay up to £20,000 a year into other ISAs, such as cash or stocks and shares ISAs, in the 2026/27 tax year. If you want to know which would suit you, I can pass you to an adviser.

The documents list these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay a maximum of £12,000 into cash ISAs each tax year. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance is unchanged, so the rest can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't advise on what you should do with your own ISAs. For that, please speak to your adviser.

Here is the answer using only what the guide says. It doesn't mention your age, so I've only stated the age bands it gives.

The guide says that from 6 April 2027, the amount investors under the age of 65 can pay into cash ISAs each tax year will be capped at £12,000. It also says "Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit." Whether that applies to you depends on your age falling in the 65-and-over band.

The guide also says money already held in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap, and that transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted. The guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Transfers are started by the receiving provider. Once we receive their request, HMRC guidelines say:

- Transfers between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days.
- Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days.
- Re-registering holdings in specie (moving them as they are) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

If your holdings are sold first and the transfer is made in cash, the proceeds move once the sales have settled. That is normally within four working days of dealing.

We don't charge for transfers in or out. To keep your ISA's tax status, use the new provider's transfer process. Don't withdraw the money. We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The documents I found don't give any further detail, such as conditions or exceptions. If you want to check how this applies to your own ISA, please raise it with your adviser. More information is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in part. A surviving spouse or civil partner gets an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

The ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. ISAs still form part of your estate for inheritance tax. The documents don't say how this would apply to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year goes over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. The total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **Tapering:** For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. This only applies if you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** If you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on how this applies to your own situation. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Here is a corrected answer using only what the earlier search returned:

"Once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions."

The documents don't say whether you can still pay in, or how this allowance applies to you. Please raise that with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Up to 25% of a pension can normally be taken tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above the allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't advise on how much you should take or when. If you'd like advice on your own situation, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment for you. We do this unless you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't tell you which option suits you. For that, please speak to an adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest. The documents don't say what the rule is for transfer values of £30,000 or less. If that's your situation, raise it with your adviser.

Based on our pensions guide:

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is separate. If you die before 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

The documents don't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Here is a corrected answer, using only what the guide says:

The pensions guide says: "Your own contributions receive tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower." It also says basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically, and higher- and additional-rate taxpayers claim the extra relief through their tax return.

The guide does not say what applies if you have no earnings at all, so I can't confirm that from it. Please raise that with your adviser. The guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Our pensions guide says unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

The annual allowance is £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. The guide doesn't say how much you personally could carry forward. Please raise that with your adviser. Guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

A full financial plan costs £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.

One-off advice on a single topic costs £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Ongoing advice costs 0.75% a year of the assets under advice. It's collected monthly from your accounts. It covers your annual review meeting, access to your adviser throughout the year, rebalancing recommendations and the quarterly reports.

If you also have discretionary investment management, both fees apply. The combined cost is set out in your client agreement.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

The annual discretionary management fee is tiered and subject to VAT:

- 0.60% a year on the first £1,000,000.
- 0.45% a year on the portion between £1,000,000 and £3,000,000.
- 0.30% a year on the portion above £3,000,000.

The documents don't give a worked total for £2m. If we provide both ongoing advice and discretionary management, both fees apply. The combined cost is set out in your client agreement and shown in pounds in your annual costs and charges statement.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the account type:

- **Model portfolios:** there are no dealing charges, including when holdings are sold to pay a withdrawal or to close an account.
- **Advisory accounts:** individual share trades cost £12.50 each.

Custody of your assets by our custodian costs 0.15% a year. More detail is on the Fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the service:

- Advice that leads to us arranging a product or investment for you is exempt from VAT.
- Stand-alone advice and discretionary investment management are subject to VAT at the standard rate.

Your client agreement states which of your fees carry VAT. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No. Fernhill Wealth is paid by fees agreed with you in advance, and we don't receive commission from product providers. Your client agreement and services and costs disclosure confirm all fees in writing before any work starts.

You can see our standard rates on the Fees and Charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Our discretionary investment management service is designed for portfolios of £250,000 or more. The documents don't say whether we accept smaller portfolios for that service.

Financial planning is available at any level of wealth. Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No, there's no charge for closing an account or for transferring out. On our model portfolios, there are also no dealing charges if holdings have to be sold.

Fund charges continue to be deducted within the funds until the holdings are transferred or sold.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The funds carry their own charges. The fund managers set these, and they're deducted within the fund. Across our model portfolios, the average ongoing fund charge was 0.21% a year at 30 June 2026.

Each April we send every client a statement. It shows in pounds all the charges paid in the previous year, including our fees, custody, dealing and fund charges. It also shows the effect they have had on your portfolio's return. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

You can complain by letter, telephone, email or in person. You can raise it with anyone in the firm. You can also contact the Client Resolution team directly:

- Email: complaints@fernhillwealth.example
- Telephone: 0117 496 0355, 09:00 to 17:30 on working days
- Post: Client Resolution, Fernhill Wealth, Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY

There is no charge for complaining, and it won't affect the service you receive. If someone complains on your behalf, we need your written permission before we can discuss your affairs with them.

**What happens next**
- If we can resolve it within three working days, we confirm that in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise we acknowledge your complaint in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it.
- We then investigate and send a final response letter.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks, we write to explain the delay and your right to go to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

More detail is on the firm's complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

Our complaints process has these timings:

- If we can resolve the complaint within three working days, we confirm that in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise, we acknowledge the complaint in writing within five working days. We also tell you who is handling it.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks of receiving your complaint, we write to explain the delay. That letter says when we expect to respond and explains your right to go to the Financial Ombudsman Service without waiting.

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter free of charge to the Financial Ombudsman Service. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response. More detail is on our complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

If you're unhappy with our final response, you can refer your complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service. This is free. You must do it within six months of the date of our final response.

- Telephone: 0800 023 4567, or 0300 123 9123
- Website: www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk
- Post: Financial Ombudsman Service, Exchange Tower, London, E14 9SR

You can also contact our Client Resolution team at complaints@fernhillwealth.example or on 0117 496 0355, 09:00 to 17:30 on working days. The documents I have don't say whether they can reopen a complaint after a final response.

The Financial Ombudsman Service's phone numbers are 0800 023 4567 and 0300 123 9123.

You can refer a complaint to them free of charge if you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response.

Four years on may not be too late. The Ombudsman can normally consider a complaint made within six years of the event. It can also consider one made within three years of when you became aware, or ought reasonably to have become aware, that you had cause to complain. Whichever of those is later applies.

If you're unsure whether your complaint is in time, contact us anyway. More information is on the complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

Five incorrect login attempts lock the account for 30 minutes. If you're still locked out after that, call the portal access helpline on 0117 496 0233. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

You can change your address in the client portal under My Details, or by secure message.

A change of name needs a certified copy of the marriage or civil partnership certificate, a deed poll, or the final order of divorce or dissolution, together with your birth certificate.

The documents I found don't say how to send these, so I can't tell you that. Please raise it with your adviser.

For a general investment account or ISA:

- **Cash already available:** we pay within five working days of your instruction.
- **Holdings need selling first:** sales normally settle within two working days of dealing. We then pay within five working days of settlement.

Pension withdrawals depend on your age and the type of pension, and tax may be payable. The Pensions page explains the options.

Valuation reports are issued quarterly. They come out within 15 working days of the end of March, June, September and December, and they are published to the client portal.

You can also ask your adviser's team for a valuation as at any date. This is normally available within two working days.

A change to the bank account we pay withdrawals to needs a signed instruction and a recent statement for the new account showing your name. We confirm the change with you by telephone on the number we hold before it takes effect. Withdrawals are paid only to a bank account in your name that we have verified in this way.

The documents I found do not say how to send the instruction and statement. Source:
https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

Yes. Paper copies by post can be arranged at no extra charge. Ask your adviser's team to set it up.

All documents are still published to the portal as well.

Yes. Interest is paid on cash balances at the rates shown on the portal. We keep a margin of 0.25% a year between the rate we receive and the rate we pay. Your client agreement discloses this margin.

Interest earned on cash outside an ISA or pension is taxable. It is reported on your annual consolidated tax certificate. From 6 April 2027 a charge will also apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares ISA. The ISA guide explains this.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Regular income is paid on the 25th of the month to your verified bank account. You can take it monthly, quarterly or annually from a general investment account or ISA.

Details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The smallest monthly direct debit you can set up is £250. Regular contributions are invested in line with your agreed portfolio on the next dealing day after we receive them.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Fund sales are placed at the fund's next valuation point and settle within four working days. Money from a sale can be paid out once settlement has taken place. So the proceeds from Monday's sale should settle within four working days of dealing.

If you then want to withdraw the money, the documents say we pay a withdrawal within five working days of settlement when holdings had to be sold first. They don't give an exact date for your sale. Details are on the Cash and dealing page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

For gains on investments sold in a general investment account, the capital gains tax annual exempt amount is £3,000. Gains above that on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income.

Losses can be set against gains in the same year. They can also be carried forward if you report them to HMRC. Income and gains inside an ISA or pension are free of UK income tax and capital gains tax.

More detail is in the tax guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Outside an ISA, dividends are tax-free up to the dividend allowance of £500 a year. Above that, they're taxed at:
- 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers
- 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers
- 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers

This is for the 2026/27 tax year. It's general information, not personal advice. You can read more in the tax guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

The consolidated tax certificate is published to the portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

No, we don't complete tax returns. Your adviser can introduce you to an accountant if you need one.

We do provide documents to help with your return. These are a consolidated tax certificate, published to the portal by the end of May each year, and a capital gains report. The certificate shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year. The report shows realised gains and losses and the figures needed for the capital gains pages of a tax return.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

A Bed and ISA means selling holdings in a general investment account and buying them back within an ISA. It uses your ISA allowance and may realise a capital gain.

There is no dealing charge for a Bed and ISA on our model portfolios. The documents don't say whether any other charges apply. Please ask your adviser about that, and about whether it suits you.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Pension transfers typically take four to eight weeks. The receiving provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, the receiving scheme carries out the checks required by the pension transfer regulations. It may require you to take guidance from MoneyHelper if the checks raise an amber flag.

We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The new provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, we deal with it.

To keep the ISA's tax status, make the transfer through the new provider's transfer process. Don't withdraw the money. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

Yes. Your documents stay available in the portal for seven years after the account closes. You can ask for paper copies at any time, and there's no charge for them.

More detail is on the closing or transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within that mandate.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which one suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will discuss both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Portfolios are managed to one of seven risk profiles. Profile 1 is the lowest risk, mainly cash and short-dated bonds. Profile 7 is the highest risk, almost entirely equities.

You agree your profile with your adviser. You do this through a questionnaire and a conversation about your capacity for loss. The profile is reviewed at every annual review. Your adviser can help you decide which one to choose.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

For a discretionary portfolio, yes. If its value falls by 10% or more since the start of a quarterly reporting period, "we tell you by the end of the working day on which it happens, as the rules require."

You also get a quarterly valuation report on the client portal. It is published within 15 working days of each quarter end. Your investment manager can talk through any report with you. The documents I found don't say how we would contact you about a fall, and they don't cover other types of portfolio.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

No. Your investments are held by our independent custodian through its nominee company, and legal title is registered in the nominee's name. You remain the beneficial owner.

Your holdings are identified to you in the custodian's records. They are kept separate from the firm's and the custodian's own assets under the Financial Conduct Authority's client assets rules. If the firm or the custodian failed and there was a shortfall, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may cover eligible claims up to £85,000 per person.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Yes. Each risk profile is available in a version that excludes companies deriving more than 10% of revenue from tobacco, controversial weapons or thermal coal, and that applies our published responsible investment policy when selecting funds.

Fees are the same as for the standard portfolios. These portfolios do not carry a sustainability label under the FCA's Sustainability Disclosure Requirements. The Responsible Investment Policy sets out the policy, the exclusion list and how we measure them. It is available on request and on the website. I don't have a direct web address for the policy itself.

Yes. Fernhill Wealth is covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS).

- **Investment business:** If we were unable to meet our obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person.
- **Cash:** Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

The FSCS website has more detail. More information is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/about-us/

Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

Separately, the FSCS covers eligible clients for up to £85,000 per person for investment business if Fernhill Wealth couldn't meet its obligations. The FSCS website has more details. My search results didn't include its address.

We have six offices: Bristol (head office), London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Leeds and Birmingham. Advisers at every office are also available for telephone and video meetings.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes. Fernhill Wealth is a trading name of Fernhill Wealth Limited, which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. You can check our authorisation on the Financial Services Register at register.fca.org.uk.

Fernhill Wealth Limited is registered in England and Wales. Its registered office is Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY.

You can read more on the Financial planning service page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

The first meeting is a free introductory appointment. It lasts about 45 minutes, carries no charge and no obligation, and can take place at any of our six offices, by telephone or by video call. At it, we explain how we work, what our services cost, and whether we think we can help. For an introductory meeting you do not need to bring anything.

If you both decide to go ahead, we send a client agreement setting out the agreed work and fees before anything is charged. To book, use the Book an Appointment page or call the new client enquiry line on 0808 157 0450.

The written plan is presented at a second meeting. That meeting is usually three to four weeks after your discovery meeting.

More detail is on the financial planning service page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

Yes. Fernhill Wealth offers one-off advice on a single topic, and consolidating pensions is one of the examples it gives. It follows the same process as our full financial planning service, on a smaller scale. The advice is confirmed in a suitability report. You can read more on our financial planning service page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

If any of your pensions are defined benefit (final salary) schemes, transferring out is treated separately. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice first. Fernhill Wealth holds the Financial Conduct Authority permission to give that advice.
